title: Promises and challenges of quantitative evaluations

cues.en: Welcome to this section of the course.
cues.zh: 歡迎來到這一章。

cues.en: Now that you have an understanding of the architecture of LMS and how they are trained and fine tuned,
cues.zh: 既然你已了解 LLM 架構，以及如何訓練與微調，

cues.en: it's time to start learning about how we evaluate trained models.
cues.zh: 現在開始學如何評估訓練好的模型。

cues.en: There are both quantitative and qualitative evaluation methods.
cues.zh: 有量化與質性兩種評估方法。

cues.en: Quantitative methods means that we can attach scores or numbers to performance and capabilities.
cues.zh: 量化，就是能對表現與能力賦予分數或數字。

cues.en: It's basically like giving a school exam to a model, and then the model gets a grade, just like you would get a grade if you were taking the exam in school.
cues.zh: 基本上像讓模型參加學校考試，再取得成績，就像你在學校應考一樣。

cues.en: Qualitative measures, which I will discuss in the next section, are ways of considering the model
cues.zh: 下一章會談質性評估，這些方法用文字與主觀評分

cues.en: output that we can describe with words and subjective ratings, but we don't really have a way to automate the evaluation.
cues.zh: 描述模型輸出，但不太能自動化評估。

cues.en: So the goal of this intro video is to explain the goals and challenges of quantitative evaluations,
cues.zh: 這支導論的目標，是說明量化評估的目的與挑戰，

cues.en: and also to introduce you to something called Goodhart's law, which you definitely need to know about
cues.zh: 也介紹古德哈特定律；研究任何技術性 AI 對齊與安全議題時，

cues.en: when studying anything related to technical AI alignment and safety.
cues.zh: 都一定要知道它。

cues.en: And it's also just a good concept to understand because it relates to economics, government, society,
cues.zh: 這也是值得理解的概念，因為除了 LLM，還涉及經濟、政府、社會、

cues.en: culture, education, and so on outside of the context of law.
cues.zh: 文化、教育等等。

cues.en: The general goals of quantitative evaluations are to have a benchmark, or actually a set of benchmarks
cues.zh: 量化評估的一般目標，是建立一個，或一組基準，

cues.en: that people can use to evaluate the capabilities of a language model.
cues.zh: 用來評估語言模型能力。

cues.en: For example, it's pretty intuitive.
cues.zh: 例如，很直覺，

cues.en: It's kind of obvious that GPT four is better than GPT two, but we would like to have some numbers that
cues.zh: GPT-4 比 GPT-2 好，似乎很明顯，但我們希望有數字，

cues.en: we can use to assess the improvements and capabilities in different models.
cues.zh: 評估不同模型能力的改善。

cues.en: Now, these benchmark numbers should reflect the capabilities of an LM, and that ranges from very basic
cues.zh: 這些基準數字，應該反映 LLM 能力，從最基礎的

cues.en: low level syntax and grammar and word usage up to world knowledge and also things like reasoning, writing,
cues.zh: 句法、文法、用詞，到世界知識，以及推理、寫作、

cues.en: code solving, math problems, knowing about details of a particular medical technique or whatever is the topic area.
cues.zh: 寫程式、解數學題，或某個醫療技術的細節等各種領域。

cues.en: Some evaluation methods are also designed to test for potentially unsafe behavior in LMS.
cues.zh: 有些方法，也會測試 LLM 潛在的不安全行為。

cues.en: For example, if a model can be tricked into telling you how to hack into someone's email account or
cues.zh: 例如，能否誘導模型說明如何駭入別人的電子郵件帳號，

cues.en: build a weapon, and we also want these evaluation benchmarks to be standardized in a way that they
cues.zh: 或製造武器。另外，也希望這些基準標準化，

cues.en: can be directly compared across different LMS, which might have different numbers of parameters or
cues.zh: 讓不同參數量、不同架構，

cues.en: different types of architecture, or developed by different organizations and companies.
cues.zh: 或不同組織公司開發的 LLM，可以直接比較。

cues.en: Again, you can think about standardized testing that is done in humans.
cues.zh: 同樣，可以把它想成人類的標準化測驗。

cues.en: So these are all the goals.
cues.zh: 這些都是目標。

cues.en: That all sounds very nice.
cues.zh: 聽起來很好。

cues.en: And wouldn't it be great if it were as simple as doing one test that gave us one perfectly accurate
cues.zh: 如果只要一個測驗，就能得到一個完全準確的

cues.en: number of all the models capabilities that we could ever use to evaluate, and we could apply it to every single LM.
cues.zh: 數字，涵蓋模型全部能力，而且適用每個 LLM，那該多好。

cues.en: Well, unfortunately, it is not quite that simple.
cues.zh: 但很可惜，事情沒那麼簡單。

cues.en: There are many challenges and limitations of these evaluation methods.
cues.zh: 這些評估方法有許多挑戰與限制。

cues.en: I will also discuss specific challenges and difficulties throughout the rest of this section.
cues.zh: 本章後面也會討論具體困難。

cues.en: And before I start showing this list here, I just want to stress that the imperfections and the flaws
cues.zh: 列出清單前，先強調：量化

cues.en: and the limitations of quantitative Evaluation metrics are not because these methods are developed by unintelligent, lazy people.
cues.zh: 評估指標的缺點與限制，不是因為開發者不聰明、懶惰。

cues.en: Quite the opposite.
cues.zh: 正好相反。

cues.en: The problem is that models language models are really complex and have multiple capabilities, some of which we don't even fully understand.
cues.zh: 問題是，語言模型非常複雜，有多種能力，有些我們甚至還沒完全理解。

cues.en: And human language is also really complex and also really ambiguous.
cues.zh: 人類語言同樣複雜，而且模糊。

cues.en: So these are fundamental challenges.
cues.zh: 所以這些是根本挑戰。

cues.en: And we have exactly the same issues with quantitative evaluations in humans.
cues.zh: 量化評估人類時，也有完全相同的問題。

cues.en: For example, even the famous SAT exam that is used in the US for getting into universities is known
cues.zh: 例如，美國用於大學入學的著名 SAT，已知對

cues.en: to have basically zero predictive ability on future life success.
cues.zh: 未來人生成功，幾乎沒有預測能力。

cues.en: And you know this yourself.
cues.zh: 你自己也知道。

cues.en: You know, whether you are a good person and whether you will have a good, productive, meaningful
cues.zh: 你是不是好人，未來能否過有生產力、有意義、

cues.en: and happy life is really not dependent on how well you can solve some particular math equation when you're 17 years old.
cues.zh: 快樂的人生，與十七歲時能解好某個數學方程式，並沒有真正的依賴關係。

cues.en: Anyway, at this point I basically just mentioned language is so complex and dynamic there are difficulties
cues.zh: 總之，這點基本上是說，語言複雜且動態，很難

cues.en: in determining what constitutes a correct answer that a model gives.
cues.zh: 判斷模型給的答案，究竟怎樣才算正確。

cues.en: You will see concrete examples of this later in the section.
cues.zh: 本章稍後會有具體例子。

cues.en: But let's say a model is supposed to predict the word chair in a sentence, but instead the model predicts the word couch.
cues.zh: 假設模型應該預測句子裡的 chair，卻預測成 couch。

cues.en: Now that is categorically incorrect, but it might still be an appropriate response given the context.
cues.zh: 類別上是錯的，但考量語境，仍可能是合適回答。

cues.en: That's just one simple example.
cues.zh: 這只是一個簡單例子。

cues.en: Relatedly, many of the eval methods are difficult or ambiguous for humans to do, and considering that
cues.zh: 同樣地，很多評估方法對人類也困難或模糊，

cues.en: these are designed to use human language, it's not really clear how well we can trust LLM performance
cues.zh: 既然是為人類語言設計，當人類自己也難以完成，

cues.en: on a language task that humans also struggle with, or at least have some ambiguity about.
cues.zh: 或至少有歧義時，我們能多信任 LLM 在這個任務的表現，也不清楚。

cues.en: Another problem is overfitting.
cues.zh: 另一個問題是過度擬合。

cues.en: Here, the issue is that once an eval method is known to AI development companies, they can start fine tuning their models on those tests.
cues.zh: 一旦 AI 公司知道某個評估方法，就能開始針對測驗微調。

cues.en: Now, even if there is some holdout set that the evaluation team keeps secret, Llms can still be fine
cues.zh: 即使評估團隊保留秘密的留出集，LLM 仍然能

cues.en: tuned to understand and perform well on the type of assessment that the evaluation method relies on.
cues.zh: 微調成理解、擅長該評估依賴的題型。

cues.en: Another issue is that open ended methods are just difficult to evaluate, and might have no real ground truth to compare against.
cues.zh: 另一個問題是，開放式方法難以評估，可能沒有可供比較的真正標準答案。

cues.en: Here you can think about the model, writing an essay, or summarizing a long text or writing some Python code.
cues.zh: 例如寫文章、摘要長文本，或寫 Python 程式。

cues.en: This point here means that you can get very different outputs of a model by prompting it in slightly different ways.
cues.zh: 這點是指，提示方式稍微不同，就可能得到很不同的輸出。

cues.en: This makes it difficult to reproduce a particular score on an eval assessment.
cues.zh: 所以很難重現某個評估分數。

cues.en: So let's say that you're trying to get the model to perform a task, and it could perform at either
cues.zh: 假設讓模型執行任務，依提示措辭不同，

cues.en: 95% accuracy or 60% accuracy, depending on the phrasing of the prompt that you use.
cues.zh: 準確率可能是 95%，也可能是 60%。

cues.en: Or maybe because of the stochastic generation of tokens, even with the exact same prompt and the same
cues.zh: 也可能因為詞元隨機生成，即使提示、模型，

cues.en: model and the same test evaluation, the performance can also vary between 60% and 90%, simply because
cues.zh: 以及評估測驗完全相同，表現也會在 60% 到 90% 間變動，單純因為

cues.en: the model is generating a new stream of tokens each time it's run.
cues.zh: 每次執行，都生成新的一串詞元。

cues.en: And finally, we have issues of cost and scalability.
cues.zh: 最後是成本與擴充性問題。

cues.en: Some eval methods are expensive and time consuming to run, and sometimes you need an expert human to evaluate the model performance.
cues.zh: 有些評估昂貴、耗時，有時需要專業人類評估表現。

cues.en: And then that can be even more expensive and time consuming.
cues.zh: 那就更昂貴、更耗時。

cues.en: Well, this here is not an exhaustive list, but just an overview of the difficulties of quantitative evaluations.
cues.zh: 這不是完整清單，只是量化評估困難的概覽。

cues.en: I hope I'm not being too critical of this field.
cues.zh: 希望我沒有對這個領域太過苛刻。

cues.en: Quantitative evaluations are super important and also really useful for helping us not only understand
cues.zh: 量化評估非常重要、非常有用，不只幫助理解

cues.en: the development and the architecture of LMS, but they also help us identify problems, flaws, and
cues.zh: LLM 的發展與架構，也能辨識問題、缺陷，

cues.en: safety risks that development companies can use to ensure not only better AI, more capable AI, but safer AI.
cues.zh: 以及安全風險，讓公司不只打造更強，也更安全的 AI。

cues.en: So my point here is just that it's really not easy to do this kind of work.
cues.zh: 我想說的是，這類工作真的不容易。

cues.en: Now I will tell you about something called Goodhart's Law.
cues.zh: 現在介紹古德哈特定律。

cues.en: It's named after a British economist and according to the Google, he looks something like this.
cues.zh: 以一位英國經濟學家命名，依 Google 顯示，他大概長這樣。

cues.en: So the quote is when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.
cues.zh: 這句話是：「當一項衡量指標成為目標，它就不再是好的衡量指標。」

cues.en: What does that mean?
cues.zh: 什麼意思？

cues.en: This means that if you are trying to improve something just by increasing the score of a particular
cues.zh: 如果只靠提高某個

cues.en: measurement, then that measurement is no longer very useful because people will just try to increase the score instead of trying to improve the thing that you are trying to measure.
cues.zh: 指標分數來改善事情，這個指標就不再很有用，因為人只會追求分數，而非改善原本想衡量的事。

cues.en: Let me go through a few examples to give you a sense of what this means.
cues.zh: 看幾個例子，就能理解。

cues.en: Imagine there are cobra snakes wild in a country and they are dangerous for children.
cues.zh: 假設某國有危險的野生眼鏡蛇，可能傷害兒童。

cues.en: So the government offers rewards for people who bring in dead cobras.
cues.zh: 政府獎勵帶來死蛇的人。

cues.en: Of course, the government had a good idea, which is to get rid of the Cobra population, but the outcome is that people start breeding cobras just to kill them.
cues.zh: 本意是減少眼鏡蛇，結果人們開始養蛇，只為殺掉領獎。

cues.en: And so we end up with even more cobras than before.
cues.zh: 最後眼鏡蛇反而更多。

cues.en: Another example is in healthcare, where hospitals are evaluated in part based on statistics like length of stay.
cues.zh: 另一個例子在醫療：醫院部分評估依據，是住院天數等統計。

cues.en: Again, this sounds great initially because the better the hospital can care for their patients, the sooner those patients will leave the hospital.
cues.zh: 一開始聽起來很好，因為照顧越好，病人越快出院。

cues.en: But what ends up happening is the patients are discharged too early when they're still sick.
cues.zh: 但結果可能變成病還沒好就被提早出院。

cues.en: Maybe they're still infectious or their injuries haven't healed yet.
cues.zh: 也許仍有傳染力，或傷口還沒癒合。

cues.en: Another example is in education, where quantitative tests are used to evaluate the school, which in turn determines how much funding the school district will get.
cues.zh: 教育也有例子，用量化測驗評估學校，再決定學區能拿多少經費。

cues.en: Again, this sounds like it should be a fair and merit based system.
cues.zh: 聽起來公平、以成果為依據。

cues.en: But the problem is that the schools just start teaching the students how to do well on the standardized test, which means that the students are not learning the skills and the knowledge that will actually
cues.zh: 但問題是，學校開始只教學生如何考好標準化測驗，導致學生沒學到真正

cues.en: help them in the future.
cues.zh: 有助未來的技能與知識。

cues.en: Now, you can see that none of these examples so far has anything to do with AI or Llms.
cues.zh: 可以看到，這些例子都與 AI 或 LLM 無關。

cues.en: Goodhart's law is not specific to AI.
cues.zh: 古德哈特定律不是 AI 專屬。

cues.en: It is a general principle in governance and economics and culture, but it is often discussed in the
cues.zh: 它是治理、經濟與文化中的一般原則，但經常在

cues.en: context of AI because models can easily be fine tuned towards basically any language based task, or
cues.zh: AI 語境討論，因為模型很容易針對幾乎任何語言任務，

cues.en: really any task that can be represented as token sequences.
cues.zh: 或任何能表示成詞元序列的任務微調。

cues.en: So let's say that tomorrow you have a genius idea for a brand new evaluation method that is really fantastic.
cues.zh: 假設明天，你靈光一閃，發明很棒的新評估方法，

cues.en: And also it's different from all the other methods that currently exist.
cues.zh: 而且不同於現有所有方法。

cues.en: So you make your evaluation method public so that everyone can use it.
cues.zh: 你公開它，讓大家使用。

cues.en: Now for the first couple of months your exam is the best eval method out there.
cues.zh: 前幾個月，它是最好的評估測驗，

cues.en: And it really highlights all the capabilities and the differences between different llms.
cues.zh: 真正凸顯不同 LLM 的能力與差異。

cues.en: The problem is that all of the companies will want their model to do really well on your test.
cues.zh: 問題是，公司都想讓自己的模型在測驗表現出色。

cues.en: So they start fine tuning their model specifically to perform well on the method that you developed.
cues.zh: 所以開始專門微調，讓模型擅長你的方法。

cues.en: And then within a half year, suddenly all these llms are doing much better on your method than they were before.
cues.zh: 半年之內，所有 LLM 突然都比以前好很多。

cues.en: And that's because the models were specifically tuned to your method, and not to whatever improvement in capabilities you thought your evaluation assessment was really measuring.
cues.zh: 那是因為模型特別針對你的方法調整，而不是你原本以為測驗衡量的能力真的改善。

cues.en: Okay, now I want to say a few words about how this section is organized in my mind.
cues.zh: 現在說明，我如何組織這一章。

cues.en: There is a hierarchy of levels of evaluation.
cues.zh: 我認為評估有層級。

cues.en: This is a hierarchy of resolution of granularity.
cues.zh: 這是解析度、細緻程度的層級，

cues.en: It's not a hierarchy of quality or importance.
cues.zh: 不是品質或重要性的層級。

cues.en: So at the finest level of granularity there are token level evaluations, which are based on looking at the model logits.
cues.zh: 最細的是詞元層級評估，查看模型 logits，

cues.en: Possibly logsoftmax transform logits.
cues.zh: 也可能先經過 log_softmax。

cues.en: And this is how you would assess the model's basic low level language skills about syntax and grammar,
cues.zh: 這能評估基礎語言能力，包括句法、文法，

cues.en: and word pair statistics like which words are likely to appear given a recent context, and so on.
cues.zh: 以及單字配對統計，例如在近期語境下，哪些詞可能出現。

cues.en: Then we have sentence level evaluation methods.
cues.zh: 接著是句子層級評估。

cues.en: Here you can think of accuracy based scores like multiple choice tests, where the model is given a
cues.zh: 可以想成以準確率為基礎的分數，例如選擇題，給模型

cues.en: couple of options with some background context, and it has to pick which option is the most correct.
cues.zh: 一些背景與幾個選項，請它挑最正確的一個。

cues.en: These kinds of measures assess the model's understanding of grammar, but it's also also its knowledge of the world.
cues.zh: 這些測驗評估文法理解，也評估世界知識。

cues.en: Because all of the options in a multiple choice test might be grammatically correct, but only one is appropriate given how the world works.
cues.zh: 因為選項的文法可能都正確，但依世界運作方式，只有一個合適。

cues.en: And then finally we have discourse level methods where we are looking at the statistical distribution
cues.zh: 最後是篇章層級方法，查看

cues.en: of token probabilities over hundreds or thousands of generated tokens.
cues.zh: 數百、數千個生成詞元的機率統計分布。

cues.en: Now, here we are not looking at the model's ability to predict the next token, or even select a correct answer.
cues.zh: 這時不看模型能否預測下一個詞元，也不只看能否選對答案。

cues.en: Instead, we are interested in whether the model is able to generate language that feels like or reads like something that a human would write.
cues.zh: 而是關注生成的語言，感覺、讀起來是否像人寫的。

cues.en: So that's it for this intro video.
cues.zh: 導論到這裡。

cues.en: I want to stress again that eval methods are a really crucial part of the development and safety of
cues.zh: 再次強調，評估方法對 AI 開發與安全

cues.en: AI, but it's just really hard to do this kind of work because it's at the intersection of multiple
cues.zh: 非常關鍵，但工作很困難，因為它位於多種

cues.en: complex phenomena, including the complexities of llms and the complexities and ambiguities of human language.
cues.zh: 複雜現象的交會處，包括 LLM 的複雜性，以及人類語言的複雜與模糊性。
